report:
Conclusion: The evidence supports a specific, interpretable difference: Model B (minus A) pushes the residual stream toward cooking/restaurant/baking/“food” vocabulary at the first few token positions (especially positions 1–4) in middle-to-late layers.

Why I believe this
- Layer/position magnitude pattern: the L2 norm of the difference is concentrated in the first few token positions (pos0–pos4), with very large spikes in middle-to-late layers (layers ~16–25). That indicates the primary behavioral difference appears early in the context window and is implemented in late-layer residual activations (where they’re most likely to affect output logits).
- Logit-lens tokens: the highest-norm cells (spread across those same layers/positions) consistently point to culinary and restaurant vocabulary: words like restaurant, Restaurant, cooking, Cooking, baking, Cake, Chef, kitchen, cooked, Chef, Baked, Cook, microwave, etc. These tokens appear repeatedly across many of the high-norm (layer, position) cells, particularly for positions 1–4 in layers ~18–25.
- Consistency across layers/positions: the same semantic cluster (food/cooking/restaurant/baking/professional/cake/chef) recurs across many adjacent layers and positions, which is a strong signal that this is a coherent domain-level shift rather than random noise.

Caveats
- There are some other tokens showing up in the logit lens (e.g., chiropractic, cadmium, dissertation, billionaire, Obama, polyurethane, metropolitan) — so the difference is not purely a single token or trivial transformation. Those could be correlated artifacts, multiple small changes, or noisy signal in some cells.
- Patchscope readouts were not provided (no continuations shown), so I cannot directly confirm that continuations produced by injecting the difference are food-themed; the inference is from the logit-lens directions and the layer/position pattern.
- I cannot say whether the change makes the model more likely to produce food-related content in real prompts (magnitude and interactions with other activations matter), only that the residual difference points strongly toward culinary vocabulary at the places and layers that typically affect next-token logits.

Short summary: The best-supported characterization is that Model B differs from A by adding activation that biases early-token logits toward cooking/restaurant/baking/food-related words (most strongly visible in late layers, positions ~1–4).
